- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model often overcorrects; cap forecast at +1.5% above true for next 3 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to avoid mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently overpredicts in early forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate late period (last 7–10 days); apply 0.5–1.5% downward correction for final 7 days if sentiment is weak or mixed.
